opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grant: New Projects and Commissions £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications £5,000; Long-Term Research grants £20,000; Research and Travel grants £2,500.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research). Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators researching and publishing on sculpture can apply for Research and Travel grants. Organisations must have been non-profit for at least 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing, conferences, lectures, publications and long-term research. Applications are considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open (closes 1 September 2026), with Winter (1 Nov-1 Dec), Spring (1 Feb-1 Mar 2027) and Summer (1 May-1 Jun 2027) rounds to follow.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses (travel: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000).

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Artists and researchers. Visiting Research Fellowships are for academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture; Artist Research Fellowships for artists developing their practice through research; Senior Fellowships (six weeks) for established scholars.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire (Studies & Gardens), including accommodation, travel and subsistence. Applications for the 2026/27 round are closed; the next round of fellowship applications will open in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; plus selected Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50, copies of dissertations added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines for a dissertation submitted within the past academic year at a UK university, relating directly to sculpture. Dissertations must not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
